record.original_question: If M is an n-dimensional parallellizable Stein manifold, can M be holomorphically immersed in C^n ? [ True for n=1 (Gunning and Narasimhan); also such an M can be immersed in C^n+1 (Eliashberg-Gromov)].

evidence.quote: Problem 9.5.1 If M is an n-dimensional parallellizable Stein manifold, can M be holomorphically immersed in Cn ? [ True for n=1 (Gunning and Narasimhan); also such an M can be immersed in Cn+1 (Eliashberg-Gromov)]. -R. Narasimhan, Dept. of Math., Univ. of Chicago, Chicago, IL 60637

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional parallelizable Stein manifold; that is, $M$ is a complex manifold of complex dimension $n$ which admits a proper holomorphic embedding into some $\mathbb{C}^N$ (equivalently, $M$ is Stein) and whose holomorphic tangent bundle $TM$ is holomorphically trivial. Does there always exist a holomorphic immersion $f \colon M \to \mathbb{C}^n$, i.e., a holomorphic map whose differential $df_p \colon T_pM \to T_{f(p)}\mathbb{C}^n$ is a (complex-linear) isomorphism at every point $p \in M$?

Known facts: for $n=1$ this holds (every open Riemann surface admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}$), and for every $n$ such an $M$ admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on holomorphic immersions of Stein manifolds (including Forstnerič's 2017 survey and subsequent work on noncritical holomorphic functions and foliations) state that the question of whether every parallelizable Stein manifold of dimension n ≥ 2 admits a holomorphic immersion into C^n remains open. Partial progress includes existence of submersions to C^{n-1} and nonsingular holomorphic foliations of intermediate dimensions, but the immersion problem into C^n itself is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic embeddings and immersions of Stein manifolds: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses open problems on immersions of parallelizable Stein manifolds into C^n.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of immersing a parallelizable n-dimensional Stein manifold into C^n is listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Noncritical holomorphic functions on Stein manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: If X is parallelizable, it admits a submersion to C^{n-1}; whether such X admits an immersion to C^n remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The question of holomorphic immersion of parallelizable Stein manifolds into C^n is still open.
